reasoning_traces.think:
The concept of insight is parsed into three core components: (1) field relationship grasping, which denotes the perception of interdependencies among elements in a problem domain; (2) means-end capacity, which formalizes the ability to navigate from a given state toward a desired outcome through structured reasoning; and (3) insight as learning, which asserts that all learning inherently includes a form of insight. These primitives are unified under a common framework where insight is not a mystical phenomenon but a computational process—specifically, the encoding of relational structures into actionable knowledge. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian updating over hypothesis spaces defined by field rules. In GSE, it appears as dynamic state transitions constrained by those same field relationships. The failure mode arises when these structures are either too complex or too abstract for current cognitive or algorithmic models to encode effectively.
